claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
label: refuted
note: Long-debunked. Fact-check coverage exists, so should hit the fast path.

claim: Humans only use 10 percent of their brains.
label: refuted
note: Neuroscience consensus. Tests whether PubMed channel contributes.

claim: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
label: refuted
note: Empirically false. Expect authority sources, no prior fact-check.

claim: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.
label: refuted
note: Refuted by published studies.

claim: Some scientists believe 5G signals cause cancer.
label: supported
note: AXIS TEST. Literally true that some individuals say this. No peer-reviewed support. A single label cannot express both.

claim: Many experts suggest that vaccines may cause long-term harm.
label: supported
note: Same shape as hd01. Tests whether the system distinguishes the existence of an opinion from its evidential backing.

claim: There are concerns that artificial sweeteners may be linked to cancer.
label: supported
note: Harder than hd01/02 — IARC did classify aspartame as possibly carcinogenic. Genuinely contested, so `contested` rather than `overstated`. VERIFY THIS LABEL CAREFULLY.

claim: Studies have raised questions about whether screen use before bed affects sleep quality.
label: supported
note: CONTROL for the hedged category — a hedge that is actually well supported. Without this, the system could pass by always saying `overstated` to hedges.

claim: Albert Einstein failed mathematics at school and published his theory of special relativity in 1905.
label: partly_supported
note: DECOMPOSITION TEST. Second half true, first half false. Requires splitting.

claim: The Great Fire of London began in a bakery in 1666 and killed thousands of people.
label: partly_supported
note: Bakery and date correct; recorded death toll was very low. Requires splitting.

claim: Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short for his time and was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
label: partly_supported
note: Waterloo correct; the height claim comes from a unit-conversion error.

claim: The Wright brothers achieved powered flight in 1903 at Kitty Hawk, having previously worked as bicycle mechanics.
label: supported
note: CONTROL for partial truths — both halves are true. Guards against a system that flags everything compound as partly supported.

claim: Pluto is the ninth planet in the solar system.
label: refuted
note: AXIS TEST. True until 2006. Supporting sources should predate refuting ones, which is what `outdated` detects.

claim: The United Kingdom is a member state of the European Union.
label: refuted
note: True until 2020. Same detection mechanism, different domain.

claim: The social media platform at x.com is called Twitter.
label: refuted
note: Renamed in 2023. More recent than od01/od02 — tests whether the temporal signal still works on a shorter gap.

claim: The tallest building in the world is the Burj Khalifa.
label: supported
note: CONTROL — a claim that SOUNDS like it should be outdated and is not. VERIFY at run time; if a taller building has completed, relabel.

claim: A Fargo, North Dakota, man was arrested for clearing snow with a flamethrower.
label: refuted
note: Originated as satire in 2013, recirculates annually. Snopes has it — fast path expected.

claim: Albert Einstein said that everyone is a genius, but if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree it will live its whole life believing it is stupid.
label: refuted
note: Misattributed quote — no evidence Einstein said it. Tests attribution checking, a very common real-world misinformation form.

claim: Finland has abolished homework in its schools.
label: refuted
note: Widely circulated distortion of Finnish education reporting. Tests amplification detection: many sources, few origins.

claim: Photographs show sharks swimming through flooded streets during a hurricane.
label: refuted
note: Recycled hoax image, recirculates after every major storm. The archetypal shallowfake.
